column1: # MemRadar Build-Cost Index: what the memory and storage for a PC build cost

column4: comment.char='#'). DuckDB: a saved copy reads as is; reading from the URL needs SET force_download=true first. Spreadsheets show these lines as text rows above the data.

column1: # WHAT THIS IS: one row per basket per month. total_usd is the sum of that basket's component medians. Each component column is the median retail price across the products MemRadar tracked in that spec that month
column2: and each _n column is how many products that median was computed over. It is a shopping basket
column3: not an index: two or three parts priced together.

column1: # BASKETS: build_current = Current build: 32GB DDR5-6000 + 1TB NVMe + 2TB NVMe; build_ddr4 = DDR4 build: 32GB DDR4-3200 + 1TB NVMe. The DDR4 basket has two components
column2: so ssd2_usd and ssd2_n are empty on its rows.

NOT A MEASURE OF CHANGE. A change computed between two rows of this file will NOT equal the MemRadar Price Index for the same period. The Price Index compares each product with itself; this file compares whichever products were tracked in each month. For how much prices changed over a period
column3: cite the Price Index at memradar.com/price-index/

column1: # SURVIVORSHIP: the tracked catalog was assembled in July 2026
column2: so historical rows contain only products still sold in 2026. They describe those products
column3: not the whole market as it stood at the time.

column1: # METHOD: only real price observations are used; days a product had no offer are excluded. Each product contributes one value per month (the median of its daily prices)
column2: so products observed more often do not outweigh the rest. A basket's series begins at the first month from which no component ever falls below 5 products; use the _n columns to apply a stricter bar. The current month is excluded until it is complete. Full methodology: memradar.com/methodology/

column1: # REGULAR PRICE ONLY: these are the everyday listed prices. Lightning Deals
column2: Prime-exclusive member prices and Warehouse prices are not in the data at all
column3: so this file says nothing about what a sale offered.

column1: # SOURCES: Amazon price history licensed from Keepa. These figures are medians computed by MemRadar from that history
column2: not the raw licensed data. Newegg prices are not included: MemRadar records Newegg as a current price only and holds no Newegg history.
